answer:
The final angular speed is  
\[
\omega=45\ \text{rev/min}
=45\frac{2\pi}{60}
=\frac{3\pi}{2}\ \text{rad/s}
\approx4.712\ \text{rad/s}.
\]
With uniform angular acceleration from rest over \(6\ \text{s}\),
\[
\alpha=\frac{\omega}{t}
=\frac{3\pi/2}{6}
=\frac{\pi}{4}\ \text{rad/s}^2
\approx0.7854\ \text{rad/s}^2.
\]

For a sticker at radius \(r\),
\[
a_{\rm tangential}=r\alpha,
\qquad
a_{\rm inward}=r\omega^2.
\]

Just before acceleration stops, \(\omega=3\pi/2\ \text{rad/s}\).

| Radius | Tangential acceleration | Inward acceleration |
|---:|---:|---:|
| \(4\ \text{cm}=0.04\ \text{m}\) | \(0.0314\ \text{m/s}^2\) \((3.14\ \text{cm/s}^2)\) | \(0.888\ \text{m/s}^2\) \((88.8\ \text{cm/s}^2)\) |
| \(11\ \text{cm}=0.11\ \text{m}\) | \(0.0864\ \text{m/s}^2\) \((8.64\ \text{cm/s}^2)\) | \(2.44\ \text{m/s}^2\) \((244\ \text{cm/s}^2)\) |

The tangential acceleration is along the direction of motion; the inward acceleration points toward the centre.

For tangential and inward acceleration magnitudes to be equal,
\[
r\alpha=r\omega^2=r(\alpha t)^2.
\]
The radius cancels:
\[
\alpha=\alpha^2t^2
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
t=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\alpha}}
=\sqrt{\frac{4}{\pi}}
\approx1.13\ \text{s}.
\]
So the two components are equal in magnitude at
\[
\boxed{t\approx1.13\ \text{s after starting}.}
\]
This occurs during the 6 s acceleration interval.

The result does **not** depend on radius, because both tangential and inward accelerations are proportional to \(r\). Therefore both stickers have their tangential and inward acceleration magnitudes equal at the same time.
